data.cultural_impact: The name Suram in Hindu culture represents strength, determination, and the ability to overcome adversity. It is a powerful name that inspires one to rise above challenges and obstacles. The name Suram is often given to children who are born into difficult circumstances, as a reminder that they have the power to overcome any obstacle with hard work and perseverance.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Suram signifies the inner warrior that resides within each individual. It is a reminder that no matter what challenges we face in life, we have the power to conquer them with the help of our spirit and inner strength. The name Suram reminds us to stay focused on our goals and to never give up, even in the face of adversity. It is a call to tap into our higher selves and to trust in our inner guidance to help us overcome any obstacle that comes our way.

historical_references.reference: Suramanshetra or Surapatana was an ancient city in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu, which is mentioned in the early Tamil literature like Agastya Purana, Purananuru and Periyapuranam. It was an important Jain center and was ruled by the Early Cholas. The temple town is believed to have been located near the present-day Thirukadaiyur.
historical_references.context: Ancient Tamil city, Jain center, ruled by Early Cholas

historical_references.reference: Suram was also a legendary king of the Chera dynasty in Kerala, mentioned in ancient Indian epics and Puranas. He was a great warrior and is said to have fought against the demon king Mahishasura. According to some versions, Suram was also known as Suran, Suranadha or Suranadar.
historical_references.context: Legendary Chera king, great warrior, fought against Mahishasura
